newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - EMI head will be a candidate to head ECB.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - EMI head will be a candidate to head ECB.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday it was premature to speculate about who might eventually head the European Central Bank (ECB) but that the head of the ECB's forerunner, the European Monetary Institute (EMI), would be a candidate for the job.
"From my vantage point this question is not an issue at the moment, the current issue is that Wim Duisenberg will succeed Alexandre Lamfalussy as head of the EMI (European Monetary Institute)."
"Later, when a decision on the members of monetary union has been reached the European Council must decide who enters the directorate (of the ECB)," Tietmeyer said.
"I can only say that the EMI president, if he has done a good job, would surely be a candidate. Unless he says he does not want the job, and he (Duisenberg) has not said that."

Responding to a question about speculation that France had proposed to Germany that Michel Camdessus -- the head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and a Frenchman -- should head the ECB, Tietmeyer said he knew of no political deals.
Tietmeyer also said that Camdessus, whom he has known for a long time, has said that he finds his current position at the IMF so important that he is not interested in giving up the post.
Tietmeyer was speaking at a news conference following a regular policy-setting council meeting.
